title: Jump Game II
statement: You start at index 0 of `nums`, and `nums[i]` is the maximum jump length from index `i`. The last index is always reachable. Return the **minimum number of jumps** to reach it.

example.why: Jump 1 step to index 1, then 3 steps to the last index.

idea: Group the indexes by **how many jumps** are needed to reach them: index 0 needs 0 jumps; the indexes it can jump to need 1; and so on. Each group is a contiguous window.
While walking through the current window, record the farthest index any of its members can reach (`farthest_reachable`). That is where the **next** window ends.
When the walk hits the end of the current window (`i == cur_end`), one more jump is unavoidable: count it and move the window end to `farthest_reachable`.

complexity.timeWhy: One pass over the array; no index is ever revisited.

steps.text: Our example: **`nums = [2,3,1,1,4]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.

steps.text: With 0 jumps we can only be on index 0, so the current window ends at `cur_end` = 0. `farthest_reachable` tracks how far **one more jump** could take us.

steps.text: From index 0 we can jump to index 0 + 2 = 2. That is the farthest so far: `farthest_reachable` = **2**.

steps.text: Index 0 was the **last index of the current window**. To go any further we must jump: `jumps` = **1**. The best jump from this window reaches index 2, so that is the end of the new window.

steps.text: From index 1 we can jump to index 1 + 3 = 4. That is the farthest so far: `farthest_reachable` = **4**.

steps.text: Index 2 was the **last index of the current window**. To go any further we must jump: `jumps` = **2**. The best jump from this window reaches index 4, so that is the end of the new window.

steps.text: The window now covers the last index. Minimum number of jumps: **2**.
